notSources.operator: Supreme Court of the United States
notSources.reason: The Supreme Court publishes opinions only as web pages and PDFs; it has no API, so reading it would mean scraping a page (tier 5, never a primary). Not added. A Polymarket market on a ruling settles on its on-chain payout instead.

Not built in sources-3 (2026-10-12). USGS gauges report stage and flow, but flood stage is an NWS threshold per gauge published by the National Water Prediction Service, so a crossing needs two publishers joined per gauge, and a gauge that stops reporting during a flood would read as no crossing. That is more than a config entry; left for a later pass.

Not built in sources-3 (2026-10-12). The best track gives positions and winds but not where a storm crossed a coast; NHC states landfalls in advisory text and in post-season reports, months later. Deciding a US landfall from positions alone would be our judgment, not the publisher's reading.

Not built in sources-3 (2026-10-12). The daily report files carry F_Scale as UNK; EF ratings come from NWS surveys and reach SPC's final database months later, so a one-shot on the next EF-N tornado cannot be read from a keyless timely feed. The tornado one-shot counts reports instead.

Not built in sources-4 (2026-10-12). A record 24-hour trading volume needs a keyless publisher whose terms allow settling on it: CoinGecko's keyless and Demo plans are for prototyping and testing, and its terms limit storing the data; CoinPaprika's free plan is personal and non-commercial with no redistribution; DefiLlama's DEX volume API sits under terms that need its written consent for commercial use and republishing. Pyth publishes values, not volumes. With no usable publisher there is nothing to read, so no rule is offered.

sources.sourceName: Helius DAS searchAssets (key) · keyless fallback: DexScreener token search + GeckoTerminal pool search
sources.cadence: continuous; one reading per complete UTC day

admission.note: ANTI-GAMING, mandatory: a mint costs ~0.002 SOL, so a bare copycat is not an event. A copycat counts only with >= $1,000 of pool liquidity or >= 25 distinct traders at the reading; one unit per creator wallet per day (the mint's first-transaction fee payer, read from RPC); at most 10 units a day; our own mint excluded; Solana only. The cheapest way to force one unit is therefore to lock >= $1,000 in a pool under a fresh wallet, and ten of them cap the day — the pool pays 1 - 0.95^10 = 40% at most, and the attacker's $10,000 of liquidity is what the coin's traders then trade against.

terms.read: CoinGecko's API Terms tie usage rights to the plan chosen; the pricing page describes the keyless public API as a way to start prototyping and the free Demo plan as good for testing and exploration, and its commercial-use section covers the paid plans only. The terms also say data may not be stored except as they permit (a cache refreshed at least every 24 hours), require a prominent Powered by CoinGecko credit, and forbid using the API for or to promote gambling. A coin's readings are kept forever on its receipts, so a keyless or Demo read cannot settle a coin. CoinPaprika, the obvious second reader, limits its free plan to personal, non-commercial projects with no redistribution, and keeps one year of daily history. With no keyless publisher whose terms allow this use, and so no cross-read either, these rules are refused at preflight.
